newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas appeals to PLO to halt talks with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hamas appeals to PLO to halt talks with Israel.

text.p: The militant Hamas movement appealed on the ninth anniversary of the Palestinian uprising on Monday for the PLO to halt peace talks with Israel and Arab countries to prepare for battle with the Jewish state.
Hamas, opposed to Arab-Israeli peace deals, renewed its "adherence to Jihad (holy struggle) as a strategic option to confront the Zionist programme in the area."

In a statement, Hamas said: "We call on the self-rule (Palestinian) Authority to stop the mockery of negotiations ...and implement its media threats to return to the popular confrontation option in order to regain its credibility."
Hamas also appealed to Arab governments to cut all ties with Israel and "start preparing for a comprehensive mobilisation programme on the basis of a battle with the enemy."
The statement marked the ninth anniversary of the start of the Palestinian uprising (intifada) against the 1967 Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Hamas was created six months after the intifada. The intifada waned after the signing of the 1993 peace deal between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).

Hamas carried out suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel last February and March. The movement, which had been the most influential Palestinian opposition group, was marginalised by a PLO crackdown following the attacks.
